2016.emphasis_summary: Excerpts are dominated by the voting overview table, a board skills matrix and committee-charter language (Science, Technology & Sustainability), with the human-capital and diversity sections empty.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: Covers 10 director nominees, a frequency-of-say-on-pay advisory proposal, and the Regulatory, Compliance & Government Affairs committee's annual review of political contributions and lobbying.
2017.notable_shifts: The director nominee slate falls from 11 to 10, executive-pay mentions triple (four to 12) and lead-director references rise from seven to 11. The human-capital and diversity sections remain empty.

2018.emphasis_summary: Presents an 11-nominee board, a say-on-pay vote, and the September 2016 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals commitment organized into five focus areas, with lead-director references at their series peak (16).
2018.notable_shifts: Lobbying references drop from four to zero and executive-pay-mix language drops from 12 to zero, while the human-capital section is populated for the first time. The lead-director count reaches its highest level in the sample.

2019.emphasis_summary: Introduces a Human Capital Management discussion of talent development and succession, and highlights a compensation recoupment policy, a policy against pledging company stock, and cybersecurity oversight in the governance highlights.
2019.notable_shifts: Clawback and recoupment mentions jump from zero to nine and peer-group mentions from three to 10, while executive pay-mix references restart (zero to seven) and perquisite references appear (zero to four).

2020.emphasis_summary: Covers board refreshment and nominee composition, the Code of Business Conduct, the ban on pledging, hedging and short-selling company stock, cybersecurity oversight, and a disclosure on drug pricing in Janssen U.S.
2020.notable_shifts: The say-on-pay discussion surfaces (five mentions, from three) and attributes the 2019 low vote to a one-time 2018 supplemental severance payment, while severance references triple (three to nine). Opioid references appear for the first time (three mentions).

2021.emphasis_summary: Dominated by COVID-19 response content, including an 'Our COVID-19 Response Efforts' section, access to vaccines and therapeutics, and Item 4 on government financial support for COVID-19 vaccines and therapeutics.
2021.notable_shifts: COVID-19 mentions surge from zero to 45 and vaccine references appear (nine, from zero), while severance references fall from nine to four.

2022.emphasis_summary: Emphasizes global equity in the COVID-19 response, an extensive review of the corporate political giving program and the Johnson & Johnson PAC, and a compensation summary in which executive pay-mix references peak at 26.
2022.notable_shifts: Lobbying references rise from zero to seven after the political-giving review, ownership-guideline references peak at 17, and COVID-19 references drop from 45 to eight.

2023.emphasis_summary: Centers on the Regulatory Compliance & Sustainability Committee and full Board review of political contributions and lobbying, alongside share ownership, clawback and peer-group pay benchmarking.
2023.notable_shifts: Executive pay-mix references fall from 26 to four and COVID-19 references disappear (eight to zero), while clawback mentions rise from eight to 10 and pay-for-performance references hold at 10.

2024.emphasis_summary: Centers on pay-for-performance and peer-group comparisons, long-term incentive and perquisite disclosure, and patient safety and product quality, with a table of contents that lists 'Pay for performance' and 'Peer group comparisons'.
2024.notable_shifts: Women-related mentions jump from one to nine and tax references go from zero to five, while AI is mentioned for the first time (two) and peer-group mentions fall from 14 to four. Lead-director references rise from seven to 15.
